title: Fixation of minimum rate of wages
legal_text: The appropriate Government shall fix the minimum rate of wages taking into account such factors as: (i) skill of workers, (ii) difficulty of work, (iii) geographical area, and other allied factors.
simplified_summary: The government will set minimum wage rates based on worker skill, work difficulty, and geographical location.

title: Time limit for payment of wages
legal_text: The wages payable to an employee shall be paid either on the expiry of the wage period or on the same day after the completion of the wage period, as daily, weekly, fortnightly or monthly basis, as the case may be.
simplified_summary: Wages must be paid right after the wage period ends, whether that period is daily, weekly, fortnightly, or monthly.

title: Rights of consumers
legal_text: The consumer shall have the right to be protected against the marketing of goods, products or services which are hazardous to life and property; to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price of goods, products or services; to be assured, wherever possible, access to a variety of goods, products and services at competitive prices; and to seek redressal against unfair trade practices or restrictive trade practices.
simplified_summary: Consumers have the right to protection from hazardous goods, clear information on product standards and pricing, access to competitive choices, and redressal against unfair trade practices.

title: Definition of unfair trade practice
legal_text: Unfair trade practice means a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or for the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice including manufacturing spurious goods, adopting deceptive pricing, or refusing to issue a cash memo or bill.
simplified_summary: An unfair trade practice involves deceptive methods, false claims, selling spurious goods, or refusing to provide bills to promote sales or services.

title: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer system, etc.
legal_text: If any person without permission of the owner or any person who is in charge of a computer, computer system or computer network accesses or secures access to such computer, computer system or computer network, downloads, copies or extracts any data, introduces any computer contaminant or computer virus, he shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person so affected.
simplified_summary: Accessing or damaging a computer network, downloading data without permission, or introducing viruses makes a person liable to pay financial compensation to the affected owner.

title: Computer related offences
legal_text: If any person, dishonestly or fraudulently, does any act referred to in section 43, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees or with both.
simplified_summary: Dishonestly or fraudulently committing acts like unauthorized computer access or data theft is punishable with up to three years imprisonment, a fine up to five lakh rupees, or both.

law_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Definition of domestic violence
legal_text: For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute domestic violence in case it harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved person or tends to do so and includes physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic abuse.
simplified_summary: Domestic violence includes any physical, sexual, verbal, emotional, or economic abuse by a respondent that harms, injures, or endangers the health, safety, or well-being of the aggrieved person.
source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

law_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Right to reside in a shared household
legal_text: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, every woman in a domestic relationship shall have the right to reside in the shared household, whether or not she has any right, title or beneficial interest in the same.
simplified_summary: Every woman in a domestic relationship has the legal right to live in the shared household, regardless of whether she owns or has a legal title to the property.
source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

title: Penalty for giving or taking dowry
legal_text: If any person, after the commencement of this Act, gives or takes or abets the giving or taking of dowry, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years, and with fine which shall not be less than fifteen thousand rupees or the amount of the value of such dowry, whichever is more.
simplified_summary: Giving, taking, or abetting dowry is punishable with a minimum of five years imprisonment and a fine of at least fifteen thousand rupees or the value of the dowry.

title: Return of amount and compensation
legal_text: If the promoter fails to complete or is unable to give possession of an apartment, plot or building in accordance with the terms of the agreement for sale, he shall be liable on demand to the allottees, in case the allottee wishes to withdraw from the project, to return the amount received by him with interest at such rate as may be prescribed, including compensation.
simplified_summary: If a builder fails to deliver possession on time as per the sale agreement, the buyer can demand a full refund of the amount paid, along with interest and compensation, or choose to continue and receive monthly interest instead.

title: Rights and duties of allottees - right to refund
legal_text: The allottee shall be entitled to claim the refund of amount paid along with interest at such rate as may be prescribed and compensation, from the promoter, if the promoter fails to comply or is unable to give possession of the apartment, plot or building in accordance with the terms of agreement for sale.
simplified_summary: Buyers (allottees) have the legal right to claim a refund with interest and compensation from the builder if the builder fails to hand over possession as promised in the sale agreement.

title: Prior registration of real estate project with Real Estate Regulatory Authority
legal_text: No promoter shall advertise, market, book, sell or offer for sale, or invite persons to purchase in any manner any plot, apartment or building in any real estate project or part of it, in any planning area, without registering the real estate project with the Real Estate Regulatory Authority established under this Act.
simplified_summary: A builder cannot advertise, market, or sell any apartment, plot, or building in a project without first registering that project with the state's Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA).

title: Wearing of protective headgear
legal_text: Every person driving or riding (otherwise than in a side-car, on a motorcycle of any class or description) shall, while in a public place, wear protective headgear of such description as may be specified by the State Government.
simplified_summary: Anyone driving or riding a motorcycle in a public place must wear a standard protective helmet.

title: Duty of driver in case of accident and injury to a person
legal_text: When any person is injured or any property of a third party has been damaged, as a result of an accident in which a motor vehicle is involved, the driver of the vehicle or other person in charge of the vehicle shall take all reasonable steps to secure medical attention for the injured person, by conveying him to the nearest hospital or medical practitioner.
simplified_summary: If a motor vehicle causes an accident injuring someone or damaging property, the driver must take reasonable steps to secure medical help for the injured person by taking them to the nearest hospital.

law_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Prevention of sexual harassment
legal_text: No woman shall be subjected to sexual harassment at any workplace.
simplified_summary: Women are legally protected from being subjected to sexual harassment at any workplace.
source: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013

title: Anti-competitive agreements
legal_text: No enterprise or association of enterprises or person or association of persons shall enter into any agreement in respect of production, supply, distribution, storage, acquisition or control of goods or provision of services which causes or is likely to cause an appreciable adverse effect on competition within India.
simplified_summary: Businesses and individuals are prohibited from entering into agreements that cause or are likely to cause an appreciable adverse effect on market competition in India.

title: Fixing hours of work for normal working day
legal_text: The appropriate Government may fix the number of hours of work which shall constitute a normal working day, inclusive of one or more specified intervals.
simplified_summary: The appropriate Government may specify the number of working hours that constitute a normal working day.

title: Wages for overtime work
legal_text: Where an employee whose minimum rate of wages has been fixed under this Code by the hour or by the day or by such a longer wage-period as may be prescribed, works on any day in excess of the number of hours constituting a normal working day, he shall be entitled to receive wages for such overtime work at a rate which shall not be less than twice the normal rate of wages.
simplified_summary: An employee who works beyond the normal working hours is entitled to overtime wages at not less than twice the normal wage rate.

title: Payment of wages after termination
legal_text: Where an employee has been removed or dismissed from service, or retrenched or has resigned from service, or became unemployed due to closure of the establishment, the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his removal, dismissal, retrenchment or resignation, as the case may be.
simplified_summary: When employment ends through dismissal, removal, retrenchment or resignation, wages payable to the employee must generally be paid within two working days.

title: Deductions which may be made from wages
legal_text: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, there shall be no deductions from the wages of the employee, except those as are authorised under this Code.
simplified_summary: An employer generally cannot deduct money from an employee's wages unless the deduction is authorised by the Code.

title: Claims under Code and procedure thereof
legal_text: The appropriate Government may appoint an authority to hear and decide claims arising under the provisions of this Code relating to payment of wages, minimum wages and other amounts due to employees.
simplified_summary: The Government may appoint an authority to hear and decide employee claims relating to wages and other amounts due.

law_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Complaint of sexual harassment
legal_text: Any aggrieved woman may make, in writing, a complaint of sexual harassment at workplace to the Internal Committee if so constituted, or the Local Committee, in such manner as may be prescribed, within a period of three months from the date of the incident.
simplified_summary: An aggrieved woman can make a written complaint of workplace sexual harassment to the appropriate committee, generally within three months of the incident.
source: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013

law_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Duties of employer
legal_text: Every employer shall provide a safe working environment at the workplace which shall include safety from the persons coming into contact at the workplace.
simplified_summary: Employers must provide a safe workplace, including protection from people encountered at the workplace.
source: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013

law_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Protection orders
legal_text: The Magistrate may, after giving the aggrieved person and the respondent an opportunity of being heard and on being satisfied that domestic violence has taken place or is likely to take place, pass a protection order in favour of the aggrieved person.
simplified_summary: A Magistrate can issue a protection order when satisfied that domestic violence has occurred or is likely to occur.
source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

law_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Monetary reliefs
legal_text: The Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence.
simplified_summary: A Magistrate may order monetary relief for expenses and losses suffered because of domestic violence.
source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

title: Penalty for demanding dowry
legal_text: If any person demands, directly or indirectly, from the parents or other relatives or guardian of a bride or bridegroom, as the case may be, any dowry, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months, but which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees.
simplified_summary: Demanding dowry directly or indirectly from the family or guardian of a bride or bridegroom is punishable under the Act.

title: Finding of District Commission
legal_text: Where the District Commission is satisfied that any of the allegations contained in the complaint about the goods or services are proved, it may issue an order requiring the opposite party to remove the defect pointed out by the appropriate laboratory from the goods in question.
simplified_summary: If a consumer complaint about a defect is proved, the District Commission may order the seller or service provider to remove the defect.

title: Refund of price paid by consumer
legal_text: Where the District Commission is satisfied that any of the allegations contained in the complaint are proved, it may order the opposite party to return to the complainant the price, or as the case may be, the charges paid by the complainant.
simplified_summary: A Consumer Commission may order a seller or service provider to refund the price or charges paid when the consumer complaint is proved.

title: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer systems
legal_text: If any person without permission of the owner accesses or secures access to a computer, computer system or computer network, or downloads, copies or extracts any data, he shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person so affected.
simplified_summary: Unauthorised access to a computer system or network, including copying or extracting data, can make the person liable for compensation.

title: Punishment for identity theft
legal_text: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
simplified_summary: Fraudulently using another person's electronic signature, password, or unique identification feature can constitute identity theft punishable under the Act.

title: Punishment for cheating by personation using computer resource
legal_text: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
simplified_summary: Cheating by pretending to be another person through a communication device or computer resource can be punished under the Information Technology Act.

title: Punishment for violation of privacy
legal_text: Whoever, intentionally or knowingly captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without his or her consent, under circumstances violating the privacy of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years or with fine not exceeding two lakh rupees, or with both.
simplified_summary: Capturing, publishing, or transmitting an image of someone's private area without consent in circumstances violating privacy is punishable under the Act.

title: Security deposit
legal_text: The security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall be such as may be agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant in the tenancy agreement, subject to the limits prescribed by the Act.
simplified_summary: The tenancy agreement may specify the security deposit, but the amount is subject to statutory limits.

title: Refund of security deposit
legal_text: The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on the date of taking over vacant possession of the premises from the tenant, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant.
simplified_summary: The security deposit must be refunded when the tenant hands over vacant possession, after lawful deductions for the tenant's liabilities.

title: Rent and receipt for payment
legal_text: Every tenant shall pay rent and other charges payable within such period as agreed to in the tenancy agreement, and every landlord or property manager shall, on receipt of payment, provide forthwith a duly signed receipt for the amount received.
simplified_summary: Tenants must pay rent according to the tenancy agreement, while landlords must provide a receipt for rent received.

title: Deposit of rent with Rent Authority
legal_text: Where the landlord refuses to accept any rent and other charges payable or refuses to give a receipt, the rent and other charges shall be paid to the landlord by postal money order or any other prescribed method, and where the landlord continues to refuse the rent, the tenant may deposit the same with the Rent Authority in the prescribed manner.
simplified_summary: If a landlord refuses rent or refuses to provide a receipt, the tenant can follow the prescribed process and may deposit the rent with the Rent Authority.

title: Recovery of rent and other charges
legal_text: If the tenant fails to pay rent and other charges within the period agreed to in the tenancy agreement, the landlord may recover the same by filing an application before the Rent Authority in the prescribed manner.
simplified_summary: If a tenant does not pay rent on time, the landlord can file an application with the Rent Authority to recover the unpaid rent and charges.
